headline: Exploited flaws in VMware vCenter and Check Point management servers need patching
plain_summary: Google says a suspected Chinese espionage group has exploited a flaw in VMware vCenter since September. GreyNoise reports a separate campaign that reached at least 22 organisations through Check Point management servers. CISA has set 26 November as the fix date for exploited flaws in N-able Mail Assure and the MONAI Label imaging tool. Organisations running these products should apply the vendor fixes now.

items.title: VMware vCenter zero-day exploited by suspected PRC espionage actor
items.why: Google says ARMORY CASTLE has exploited an unauthenticated authentication bypass, CVE-2026-123890, since early September 2026.
items.action: Google advises applying Broadcom's patches immediately; SecurityWeek lists fixed builds 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200 and says 7.0 has no public patch.

items.title: GT13 campaign hits Check Point Security Management Servers
items.why: GreyNoise says at least 22 organisations were affected between October 17 and November 2, and it does not attribute the actor to any known group.
items.action: Check Point advises installing its jumbo hotfix for CVE-2026-16232 and restricting Trusted Clients and Management access to trusted IP addresses.

items.title: MONAI Label zero-day exploited by AI agents; CISA deadline 26 Nov
items.why: Amazon says AI agents exploited a path traversal flaw and gained root on a server, and attributes it to a Chinese-nexus actor with moderate confidence.
items.action: ENISA's record lists MONAI Label versions before 0.8.6 as affected; follow the maintainers' advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94.

items.title: N-able Mail Assure and SpamExperts server accessed; CISA deadline 26 Nov
items.why: N-able says one hosted server was accessed and found no evidence customer data was compromised; it has not said whether CVE-2026-134624 was the way in.
items.action: SpamExperts Local Cloud operators should confirm they run build 20261121.1943; Hosted Cloud users have nothing to install.

items.title: CISA adds SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-42884 to exploited catalog
items.why: CISA lists the Enterprise Portal JNDI injection, rated CVSS 6.5, based on evidence of active exploitation.
items.action: General advice: confirm SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal has the fix SAP released in its November 2025 Patchday.

items.title: F5 BIG-IP flaw CVE-2026-126714 has public proof-of-concept code
items.why: HKCERT says an authenticated remote attacker could run system commands; the event does not report exploitation in the wild.
items.action: HKCERT advises applying the workarounds in F5 advisory K000164320 for BIG-IP 17.1.0 - 17.1.3, 17.5.0 - 17.5.1 and 21.1.0.

items.title: Prism Medical Products breach affects 1,326,066 people
items.why: An Oregon filing gives the count; HIPAA Journal, not the company, says it appears to be Wallstreet ransomware.
items.action: Prism Medical Products is mailing notification letters and offering 24 months of credit monitoring and dark web monitoring, per HIPAA Journal.

items.title: South Korea drafts no-fault liability for digital asset operators
items.why: The FSC draft would make operators liable for hacking losses even without negligence, with a surcharge capped at 10% of sales.
